speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: asked the Minister for National Development in the recent HDB Build-To-Order (BTO) and Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) launch in July 2025, (a) what is the success rate for first-time applicants who are eligible for the Family Care Scheme (Proximity); and (b) what is the breakdown of successful applicants based on their number of prior unsuccessful attempts.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I just wanted to give some context in terms of my supplementary question.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The reason why I asked this is I have seen several appeals with regard to the launch of the Simei Symphony that is part of that launch.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Many families were coming to appeal because they do want to stay with their families.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I noted Minister's point about the numbers in terms of those who had a queue number because I had several residents who came to see me who had many more attempts, some with three or four attempts at BTO applications, and were not successful.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: To give the context, for inter-generational caregiving needs, many do want to stay within the area, not just in Simei, for my residents of course, but even in the East they have been applying.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Given that these proximity schemes or other priority schemes are giving residents more ballot opportunities, would the Ministry of National Development consider refinement to the balloting process that would allow the Proximity Scheme to give real priority for those who have attempted several times within an area that is close to their family, or may be, perhaps, even in extending the proximity area, may be beyond the four kilometre?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Indeed, we do want to encourage more families to stay near their family members, whether parents or children, so that the family can provide mutual support to one another.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: HDB offers a range of priority schemes to enhance the ballot chances of certain groups.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Please allow me to just share a little bit with the House.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For example, all first-timers receive one additional ballot.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: First-timer parents and married couples, eligible families receive an additional ballot.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In other words, three ballots in total if they apply for a 4-room or a smaller standard flat.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, we do want to help them if they continue to apply for a standard flat, 4-room or smaller, to keep increasing their chances if they are unsuccessful.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: On top of this, we give priority also under various schemes to further enhance chances of various groups.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And the purpose is to support young parents and those who wish to live near their parents.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Those who qualify for both schemes would be balloted twice.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Those who are unsuccessful in both ballots are then balloted again as a first-time, public applicant.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, we offer higher chances to certain groups of buyers but to be candid, balloting outcomes cannot be guaranteed because there is an element of luck.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is especially so in popular projects, like the one that Ms Tan mentioned, and also in the larger flats such as 5-room flats or SBF flats, which the supply is smaller but the demand is high.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And we want to encourage applicants to also consider applying for projects where there are larger supplies because the application rate would then be better.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: During the application process, the application rates by estate and flat type would also be provided online and updated multiple times a day.
